name: Leadership
essenceStatement: The Spirit-given capacity to direct, mobilize, and care for others toward what God is doing in his Kingdom.
workingDefinition: The Spirit-given capacity to direct, mobilize, and shepherd others toward Kingdom purpose. Paul's word in Romans 12:8 is proistemi -- 'to stand before,' to lead, to take the front. The gift of leadership in the New Testament always carries the dual call of direction and care: the leader who directs without caring is a manager; the leader who cares without directing is a chaplain. The gift in its full New Testament form is the believer who carries both -- who sees the Kingdom path forward and brings others with them toward it. For high-scoring believers whose responses indicate pioneering or apostolic gifting (the call to plant new works, take new ground, or lead the church into new territory), the formation output addresses this dimension specifically. Apostleship as the New Testament names it is folded into Leadership in this instrument, with the pioneering function emerging in the formation output rather than as a separate gift category.
diagnosticChallenge: Leadership is easily confused with executive ability, charisma, or natural authority. The naturally commanding person may direct others effectively without ever functioning in the gift; the talented executive may build organizations without Spirit-given empowerment for Kingdom leadership. The signature of the gift is that the leader's direction produces movement toward what God is doing, not just toward what is strategic, profitable, or scalable. The gift is also distinguished by its pastoral component: the New Testament leader cares for those they lead, not just deploys them.

manifestationWitnesses.text: Then I told them of the hand of my God that had been upon me for good, and also of the words that the king had spoken to me. And they said, 'Let us rise up and build.' So they strengthened their hands for the good work.
manifestationWitnesses.note: Nehemiah at Jerusalem -- the gift of leadership in its most complete biblical form. Nehemiah saw what God was doing, mobilized the people, sustained them through opposition, and built the walls in fifty-two days. He combined vision with execution, direction with care for the workers, urgency with prayer. The gift produces movement that the body could not produce without it.

manifestationWitnesses.text: After they finished speaking, James replied, 'Brothers, listen to me. Simeon has related how God first visited the Gentiles to take from them a people for his name... Therefore my judgment is that we should not trouble those of the Gentiles who turn to God...'
manifestationWitnesses.note: James at the Jerusalem Council -- the gift of leadership operating in a moment that could have split the early church. James listened, discerned, and named the path forward. The body received his leadership because he had earned it through faithful service, careful discernment, and a heart for the unity of the church. Leadership as a gift functions through trust earned over time.

stewardshipCharge.text: You know that those who are considered rulers of the Gentiles lord it over them, and their great ones exercise authority over them. But it shall not be so among you. But whoever would be great among you must be your servant, and whoever would be first among you must be slave of all. For even the Son of Man came not to be served but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many.
stewardshipCharge.note: The most direct stewardship charge in scripture. Christian leadership inverts the world's pattern. The Kingdom leader serves those they lead. The gift, exercised faithfully, will cost the leader more than it costs those they lead. Any leadership that drifts toward the world's model of authority has drifted away from the gift's New Testament shape.

inclinationQuestions: When I am part of a group, ministry, or initiative without clear direction, I find that others naturally look to me to provide it -- and what I offer tends to bring focus and movement, not just opinions.
I see what God is doing or could do in situations the body is facing, and I can articulate a path forward in ways that mobilize others to act on it.

I am willing to carry the weight of leading -- the responsibility, the disappointment, the visibility, the cost -- because I believe what is being built matters, and I find that others trust me to bear that weight on their behalf.
fruitfulnessQuestion: When you have led a group, initiative, or ministry, how often has it produced visible Kingdom fruit -- people grew, the work advanced, the body was built up -- rather than producing motion without growth or visibility without substance?
communityConfirmationQuestion: When [Name] is in a leadership role, the group or initiative they lead consistently moves toward real Kingdom outcomes -- people grow, work advances, the body is strengthened -- and the people they lead feel cared for, not just directed.

bodyApplication.where: Leadership functions in pastoral roles, elder boards, ministry directorships, small group leadership, missions teams, parachurch ministry, church planting, men's and women's ministry, and the workplaces and communities where believers carry Kingdom influence. It also operates in less formal settings -- the believer who organizes the prayer initiative, the parent who shepherds their family well, the member who consistently moves things forward in their congregation without holding office.
bodyApplication.whatItLooksLike: The believer whose leadership produces both Kingdom advance and pastoral care. The pastor whose church grows in maturity, not just attendance. The ministry director whose team develops as disciples while accomplishing the mission. A leadership-gifted believer functioning well is willing to bear the cost of leading -- the disappointments, the criticism, the weight of decision -- and treats those they lead as people first, workers second. Their leadership produces multiplication: other leaders emerge under them, gifts develop, the body grows.
bodyApplication.distortions: This gift, when distorted, produces the most damaging dynamics in the church. It can become control: the leader who directs without caring, who treats those they lead as resources to be deployed. It can become charisma without substance: visibility, attention, and platform without the actual fruit of disciples being formed. It can become abuse: the use of leadership authority to manipulate, silence, or harm those who serve under it. The most insidious distortion is the slow drift into the world's model of leadership -- where Christian language is layered over hierarchical authority, executive efficiency, and personal ambition. Jesus's words in Mark 10:42-45 are the corrective.
bodyApplication.pairings: Leadership functions alongside Administration (which provides the operational structure to execute vision) and Shepherding (which provides the pastoral care that protects leadership from becoming command without care). The leadership-gifted believer who lacks administrative support struggles to execute; the one who lacks shepherding instinct can lead effectively but leave wounded people in their wake.

formationOutput.active:
The Spirit's work through you in leadership is to see what God is doing, mobilize others toward it, and carry the weight of bringing them with you. This is what Nehemiah exhibited at Jerusalem and what James exhibited at the council. The gift in its New Testament form always carries the dual call of direction and care: you are responsible for the work and for the people doing it.

The stewardship of this gift is one of the heaviest in scripture. The world's model of leadership is constantly available to you, and the slow drift toward it is the chief temptation of every Christian leader. Jesus's command in Mark 10 is the controlling framework. Christian leadership inverts the world's pattern. The leader serves; the leader bears the cost; the leader treats those they lead as people first. Hold this standard close, because the gift is rarely lost in a single moment of failure -- it is lost in a thousand small drifts toward control, toward platform, toward executive efficiency at the expense of pastoral care. Stay close to the people you lead. Listen to their voices, especially the dissenting ones. Submit your leadership to elders and accountability structures. And remember that the gift is measured by the maturity of those formed under your leadership, not by the size or visibility of what you built.

For believers whose responses indicate pioneering or apostolic gifting: If you find yourself drawn not to leading existing ministries but to starting new works, taking new ground, or pioneering where the church has not yet gone, the Spirit may be developing the apostolic dimension of this gift in you. The early church's pattern in Acts 13:1-3 is the framework -- the Antioch church set apart Barnabas and Saul under the Spirit's direction for the work. The pioneering call is not self-appointed. It is recognized, commissioned, and sent by the local church under the Spirit's leading.
formationOutput.anchorScriptureText: But whoever would be great among you must be your servant, and whoever would be first among you must be slave of all.
formationOutput.weeklyPractice: This week, identify one person under your leadership -- in any sphere where you lead -- and spend time with them not directing but listening. Ask them what they are facing. Ask them how they are. Ask them what you could do differently. Receive their answer without defense. The gift of leadership is sharpened by the discipline of being led by the people you lead, listening to their voices, and adjusting based on what you hear.

edgeCases.emerging: Your responses suggest the Spirit may be developing this gift in you, but consistent fruit of Spirit-led leadership has not yet emerged. Test the gift in one specific context -- a small group, a ministry team, a workplace initiative. Lead with both direction and care. Submit your leadership to mature, accountable oversight. After a season, ask the same trusted people whether they have seen the gift functioning. Leadership in its New Testament form is forged slowly, under accountability, through faithful service.
edgeCases.inclinationConfirmationGap: You sense yourself drawn to lead, but the people who know you well have not seen consistent Kingdom fruit from your leadership. This is one of the most important findings the instrument can surface. The inclination toward leadership is often confused with personality traits -- the ambition, the executive instinct, the desire for visibility -- that resemble the gift without producing its fruit. Take this gap seriously. Submit your sense of this gift to a mature, accountable mentor. Lead under their oversight. Watch carefully whether your leadership produces the maturity of disciples formed and the body strengthened, or whether it produces motion without growth.
edgeCases.confirmationInclinationGap: Two or more of the people who weighed in see leadership in you that you did not claim. This is significant. The believer who carries leadership in its New Testament form often does not name themselves a leader -- they simply serve and find others following them. Worth taking seriously. Submit this finding to your pastor or trusted elders. Pay attention to the ways others may already be looking to you for direction. The body may be telling you something the Spirit is doing through you.
edgeCases.quiet: This gift is not where the Spirit is most visibly working through you in this season. That is information, not deficiency, and given the unusual weight this gift carries, its absence is no thing to grieve. Trust the leadership-gifted believers in your community to provide direction in their spheres, follow them well, and look to the gifts where the Spirit is more clearly at work in you.
